taxonomy.rationale: Agents are NOT classified by single- vs multi-agent architecture. That describes implementation, not research position, and it cannot explain why post-exploitation is uncovered. The two axes used here — original design intent and evaluation target — between them determine whether the post-exploitation phase could have been measured at all, which makes the classification itself part of the argument.

axes.design_intent: What the system was built to achieve.
axes.eval_target: The environment in which it was actually validated.

G1.label: Academic-benchmark oriented
G1.intent: Raise the success rate on an existing benchmark and offer a mechanism as the contribution.
G1.target: XBOW / VulHub / VulnHub / CTF — mostly web-application layer or single host.

G2.label: Real-environment validation
G2.intent: Reject synthetic benchmarks; require a live testbed.
G2.target: Enterprise network or Active Directory range.

G3.label: Production tooling
G3.intent: Let more people, or the same people better, run real red-team work.

G4.label: Single-vulnerability proof
G4.intent: Finding and PROVING one vulnerability completes the task.

bottleneck_codes.B1: Out of scope — the phase is absent from the system's own task definition.
bottleneck_codes.B2: Unmeasured — no multi-host target, so capability is unknown either way.
bottleneck_codes.B3: Measured and failed — the only category that can support a capability claim.

model_stance_codes.capability-first: Picks the strongest available closed model, to show the task CAN be done.
model_stance_codes.cost-first: Deliberately picks open weights, to show the task does NOT require a frontier model.
model_stance_codes.model-as-subject: Sweeps many backends; the model is the independent variable, not a tool.
model_stance_codes.byo-llm: Repo-only product: the model is the user's choice, so it is not a research decision.
model_stance_codes.not-disclosed: The model actually used is not published.

honest_boundaries: Convenience sample (public artefact, 2024 onward, retrievable at survey time) — not exhaustive.
VulnBot and Pentest-R1 share a laboratory and authors — not independent samples.

Vigolium and OpenHack are arguably better excluded from any coverage denominator: post-exploitation is absent from their task definition, so counting them turns a scope difference into a capability decay.
Parameter counts for the repo-only group are hardcoded defaults, NOT experimental models — do not pool the two groups.
Per-agent B1/B2/B3 adjudication exists only for the batch that was examined for it; other agents carry null.
